qt: to the Commission Alvise Pérez (NI) Subject:

According to Spain’s General Comptroller of the State Administration (IGAE), as of 31 August 2026 the payments of EU housing provisions budgeted between 2024 and 2026 amounted to 901.4 million out of 6 987.8 forecasted: 12.9 %1 2. Spain has 8 132 municipalities compared to 342 in the Netherlands, 308 in Portugal, 290 in Sweden and 98 in Denmark. Castile and Leon, with 2 248, has over double what those four countries have combined. The multiplication of municipalities calls for an assessment of whether there are enough specialist staff to process land, licences and procurement, and whether metropolitan planning would allow investments to be implemented with lower administrative costs and delays. The government of Pedro Sánchez must explain why its housing promises do not translate into verifiable results. The dispersion of town planning competences, repeated procedures and overlapping political structures need to be examined as potential obstacles, especially for young people. EU funding should finance housing, not sustain duplications, inefficient local councils or unjustified positions of trust. 1.
What final implementation and reaching of milestones does Spain demonstrate in housing?
Will the Commission assess the impact of municipal fragmentation on licences, costs and EU projects, comparing it with these states according to population, territory and competences?
Will the Commission provide recommendations and technical assistance for voluntary mergers and metropolitan management, while respecting national competences and local self-government?
